VS Code extension · Copado · GitHub

Release Overlap Inspector

Bundling a release from UAT with Copado's User Story Bundling can carry future-release changes into production. The inspector shows you which components are at risk, and what changed, before you deploy.

The problem

How an unapproved change reaches production

It happens in five steps, and none of them looks wrong on its own.

  1. Our releases are large

    A release often carries 300 or more user stories. Each story has its own feature branch and changes its own set of components: classes, flows, profiles, permission sets.

  2. One big promotion takes a whole day

    If we put all 300 stories into a single promotion, Copado merges them one after another and raises merge conflicts story by story. Each conflict has to be resolved before the next story goes in. On a release this size, that can take a whole day.

    Story 37 of 312 · conflict in Test_FlowResolve, then continue

  3. So we bundle from UAT

    Once the stories are in UAT and ready for production, we use Copado's User Story Bundling. All 300 stories become one bundle story, and we resolve every conflict once, in one place. The bundle gets its metadata by retrieving it from UAT.

    → 1 bundle story Conflicts are resolved once for the whole release.

  4. UAT holds more than our release

    UAT is shared. Releases planned for later are deployed there too, so they can be tested. A Salesforce org keeps only one version of each component. When our release and a future release change the same component, UAT holds one version that contains both changes.

    DEV
    QA
    UAT
    PROD
    Test Release 01approved
    going out now →
    Test 27-11 01future
    not approved
    SampleUtility.cls

    Both releases touched SampleUtility, so the copy in UAT carries both changes.

  5. The bundle can't tell the changes apart

    The bundle retrieves each component from UAT as a whole file. It takes our change and the future release's change together. No deployment fails and nothing warns you, so a change that is not approved for production yet might get deployed.

    SampleUtility.cls · as retrieved from UATExample
    public with sharing class SampleUtility {    public static String greet(String name) {        return 'Hello, ' + (String.isBlank(name) ? 'World' : name);    }     public static Integer addNumbers(Integer a, Integer b) {        return (a == null ? 0 : a) + (b == null ? 0 : b);    }     public static Boolean isEven(Integer value) {        return value != null && Math.mod(value, 2) == 0;    }}
    Our release (approved)US-0004815 · Test 27-11 01 (not approved)

    Any shared component is a risk.

    It doesn't matter that the two releases changed different lines. The bundle takes the whole file, so the future change goes with ours.

The trade-off

One promotion or a bundle

Bundling saves a day of conflict fixing, but it changes where the metadata comes from.

One promotionUser Story Bundling from UAT
Merge conflictsRaised story by storyResolved once for the whole release
Time on a 300-story releaseCan take a whole dayMuch less
Where the metadata comes fromEach selected story's own commitsWhatever is in UAT at that moment
What can reach productionOnly the stories you selectedChanges from any release deployed in UAT

Why checking by hand doesn't hold up

It's slow

You export the components of every story in both releases and match them in a spreadsheet. On 300 stories that takes hours.

It goes stale

Future releases keep deploying to UAT. Yesterday's comparison misses today's stories.

It stops at the name

A match tells you a component is shared. It doesn't show what the other story changed or whether anyone reviewed it.

The answer

What the inspector tells you

Pick the release going out and the future releases in the org. In seconds you get four answers.

SHARED COMPONENTS

Which components does my release share with future releases?

Every overlap, grouped by metadata type, with a search box to find one by name.

RISK LEVEL

Which overlaps are risky?

Each component is marked Needs review, Check or Clear, based on how many future stories touch it and whether their changes have a PR.

PR DIFF

What exactly did the other story change?

One click opens the story's change side by side in VS Code, from its promotion PR or its feature PR.

TARGET ENVIRONMENT

What's in the org I'm bundling from?

Choose trnqa, trnUat or any environment to see the promotions that actually went into it.

One-time setup

Setup

You need three things on your machine. Most Salesforce developers have them already.

VS Code 1.80+

The inspector opens as a VS Code panel.

code --version
Salesforce CLI

Logged in to the org where your Copado releases live, such as CopadoGov.

sf org list
Git with GitHub access

Access to the story repos, so the inspector can fetch PR commits for the diffs.

git --version

  1. Log in to the Copado org

    Skip this if the org already shows in sf org list.

    sf org login web --alias CopadoGov

  2. Get the install file

    Download sf-release-conflict-checker-1.1.0.vsix from the Release-Conflict-Checker repository on GitHub, or ask the team for it.

  3. Install it

    In VS Code open Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X), click the … menu, choose Install from VSIX… and pick the file. Or run this from the folder that holds it:

    code --install-extension sf-release-conflict-checker-1.1.0.vsix --force

    Then run Developer: Reload Window. To update later, install the newer file the same way.

  4. Open the inspector

    Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run SF: Release Overlap Inspector.

Every release

Run a check

Fill in the panel on the left from top to bottom, then click Analyse.

  1. 1
    Salesforce orgType or pick the CLI alias of your Copado org and click Connect. The releases load below.
  2. 2
    ModeBy release compares whole releases. By user story compares two stories by name.
  3. 3
    PR sourcePromotion uses PRs from completed promotions into the target environment. Use it when you bundle from an org. Feature branch uses each story's own PR.
  4. 4
    Target environmentNext environment (auto) follows each story's next step. Pick a fixed environment, such as trnUat, to match the org you bundle from.
  5. 5
    Releases to promoteGreen. Tick the release that's going out now.
  6. 6
    Future planned releasesAmber. Tick the releases deployed in that org that are not going out with yours.
  7. 7
    Analyse common componentsRuns the check in seconds. The first run on a repo takes longer while it clones the repo once.

Results

Read the results

Start with the counts at the top, then work through the red components first.

  1. 1
    Summary cards8 shared components, 1 future release affected, 8 future-release stories, and 7 stories whose change has no promotion PR.
  2. 2
    Risk tallyHow many components are Needs review, Check and Clear. Hover for the rule behind each.
  3. 3
    SearchType part of a name to filter the list. It shows how many match, such as "1 of 8".
  4. 4
    Components by typeThe dot shows the risk. The number is how many future-release stories touch that component.
  5. 5

  6. 6
    PR DiffOpens what that story changed in the component, side by side in VS Code.

What the colours mean

Needs review

2+ stories · a PR missing

Several future stories changed it, and at least one change was never reviewed in a PR.

Check

2+ stories, all with a PR
or 1 story · no PR

The overlap is smaller, or every change was reviewed. Still look before you bundle.

Clear

1 story · has a PR

One future story, and its change was reviewed. A quick look at the diff confirms it.

Act on it

Act on a finding

Open the change, decide whether it can go to production, and settle it before you deploy the bundle.

Needs review

Do thisOpen each story's change. Talk to the owners of the future stories. Agree whether their change can go out with yours, or take it out of the bundle before you deploy.

Check

Do thisOpen the diff and confirm the change is safe to ship. If you're unsure, ask the story owner.

Clear

Do thisOpen the PR diff and confirm in a few seconds that nothing surprising rides along.

See exactly what changed

PR Diff shows only what the story's merge brought into the promotion branch, or with the Feature branch source, only the story's own commits. Use #N to open a single PR, or All PRs Diff to combine them. With no PR, Branch Diff compares the feature branch with its base.

Check the org you're bundling from

Help

Troubleshooting

The org doesn't connect, or no releases load

Run sf org list and check the alias is listed and connected. If the login has expired, run sf org login web --alias <alias> again.

The first analysis is slow

The first time it meets a repo, the inspector clones it into VS Code's storage. Later runs only fetch new commits. Progress shows in the Release Overlap Inspector output channel.

"Could not clone" error

Your Git login doesn't have access to that GitHub repo. Check you can open the repo in GitHub, then sign Git in again.

A story says "No promotion PR"

That's a finding, not an error. The story hasn't been promoted into the target environment yet, or its promotion merged without a PR. Treat the change as unreviewed.

A component I expected is missing

Check the right future releases are ticked and the story's metadata is committed in Copado. The inspector compares the components Copado records on each story.
